inventory.description: Pure, host-testable products of Packages/VisualCore: VisualCoreMath, VisualCoreSimulation, VisualCoreScenes, VisualCoreShaderSource, VisualCoreEffectsGraph, VisualCoreDiagnostics, VisualCoreAudioDSP, VisualCorePersistence, VisualCoreParameters, VisualCoreExperience (+ VisualCoreTestSupport for test targets). iOS products of Packages/VisualCoreRendering: VisualCoreRendering, VisualCoreEffects, VisualCoreUI, VisualCoreAudio, VisualCoreAutomation, VisualCoreExperienceHost. For Living Wallpapers (checked 2026-11-17): VisualCoreRendering has RenderHost.renderOffscreen(width:height:time:) with maxRenderSize and maxOffscreenPixels (64,000,000), StillImage, OffscreenRenderError, StillImageEncoder.pngData (opaque PNG tagged sRGB, the only encoder) and StillCapture (one PNG in a temporary folder, nothing written to Photos), render targets with readPixels, CachedScene, CrossfadeScene, FullScreenShaderScene, FieldPass and ShaderBundle with the vc/ GLSL library; VisualCoreEffects has EffectScene; VisualCoreExperienceHost has ExperienceSession.renderStill (always at time 0) and the experienceStillRenderer environment value; VisualCoreScenes has ExportGeometry (hardMaxEdge 8192, defaultMaxPixels 64,000,000), ExportAspect (square, 4:5, 16:9, 9:16) and ExportSize; VisualCoreDiagnostics has ResourceBudget; VisualCorePersistence has TemporaryFolder; VisualCoreExperience has ExperienceStorage with StorageQuota (16 MiB, 64 files). Missing in every framework product (grep 2026-11-17): a JPEG or HEIC encoder or any colour space but sRGB, any video encoding (no AVAssetWriter, pixel buffer or VideoToolbox use), tiled rendering, a device screen-size and safe-area catalog, an export job with progress, and an offscreen still of an experience at a chosen time.

inventory.area: EGL render host and its main-thread rule
inventory.description: RenderHost (@MainActor) owns the EGL display, context and surfaces over ANGLE's Metal backend (EGLDisplayProvider), the CAMetalLayer RenderView, the FrameScheduler (CADisplayLink with FramePacing) and context generations; every GL call runs on the main thread inside RenderScene setup, resize, render and teardown, and renderOffscreen asserts the main thread. RenderHost pauses on background, resumes on foreground, rebuilds on memory warning and recreateContext, and swaps scenes with replaceScene. RenderCapabilities reports maxTextureSize, maxRenderbufferSize and maxViewport and records findings below the OpenGL ES 3.0 floor of 2048; maxRenderSize is the smallest of those limits (0 before a context reported them). The offscreen render is synchronous on the main thread: it validates the size before any GPU work, renders into a registry render target, reads the pixels back top-down, and on every path releases the target, rebinds framebuffer 0 and resizes the live scene back.

inventory.area: Shaders and resources (full-screen shaders, fields, palettes, render targets, the offscreen path)
inventory.description: FullScreenShaderScene draws one bundled fragment shader over the canvas with named float uniforms, a palette of up to 8 colour stops, seed offsets and an explicit fixedTime; FieldPass runs a fragment program into a render target or the framebuffer (PingPongTarget for feedback); ShaderBundle and ShaderLibrary compile bundled GLSL with #include of the vc/ library (palette, noise, sdf, hash, colour, field); ResourceRegistry.makeRenderTarget creates RGBA8 render targets under a ResourceBudget and RenderTarget.readPixels reads them back; RenderContext.redirected points a scene at another framebuffer and size, which is how renderOffscreen draws at an output size independent of the screen.

EffectScene wraps a content scene in an EffectGraphDescription run by EffectRenderer (post passes, a flash limiter under Reduce Flashing, a bypass); CrossfadeScene mixes two scenes through render targets; CachedScene keeps a child's picture until its key changes. All three are RenderScenes, so renderOffscreen draws them at output size (CrossfadeSceneTests render offscreen).

ExportGeometry clamps a long edge to min(maxEdge, 8192), even, and a pixel cap, and sizes ExportAspect presets into ExportSize; StillCapture renders through renderOffscreen, encodes with StillImageEncoder.pngData and keeps only the latest PNG in a TemporaryFolder; ExperienceSession.renderStill(width:height:) is the experience's still on the session's host at time 0, handed to controls as the experienceStillRenderer environment value. Experience-only consumers: the Transferable PNG files shared with SwiftUI ShareLink by Generative Art Studio (ExportSheet), Fluid Art Playground, Fractal Explorer, Infinite Geometry and Simulation Lab (SimulationCapture); no experience calls PhotoKit.

project.yml gives the one app NSPhotoLibraryAddUsageDescription (add-only, 'Save Image' in the share sheet); Configs/permission-vocabulary.json maps the permission word photo-library-add to that key and text; each registration in Catalog/registrations.json declares its words (only a01.generative-art-studio declares photo-library-add today); scripts/check_usage_descriptions.py, run by the release steps usage-descriptions and app-usage-descriptions, requires the app's usage keys to equal the union of the declared words. Saving to Files or another app through the share sheet needs no permission.

DocumentStore writes versioned documents (DocumentEnvelope kind and schemaVersion) atomically under a byte cap and migrates them through a MigrationChain; NamedLibrary keeps named documents with favourites; ExperienceStorage is the experience's own folder bounded by StorageQuota (16 MiB, 64 files); TemporaryFolder makes and removes temporary files for exports.

ExperienceSession opens, checkpoints, closes and recovers an Experience on one RenderHost, applies quality (QualityGovernor over the QualityProfile, fed by DeviceConditions), memory-warning and scene-phase events, keeps a PerformanceRecord and renders the experience's still; ExperienceShell adapts an ExperiencePresenter (scene, controls, canvas overlay through makeCanvasOverlay) and supports cancelPreparation; ExperienceEngine.prepare runs the core's preparation with an optional time limit; the one app registers experiences in ExperienceRegistry and Catalog/registrations.json (eighteen registered, A01-A18, checked 2026-11-17; Living Wallpapers joins in A19-P01 and stays unregistered and unavailable in A19-P00; scripts/check_experience_packages.py forbids unregistered targets).

XcodeGen spec project.yml for the one app (target VisualCore), package schemes via scripts/xcodebuild_package.py, app tests via scripts/xcodebuild_app.py, and scripts/release_check.py: 148 named steps listed by --list on 2026-11-17 (shared checks including app-contracts, which checks every docs/apps/*/visualcore-contract.json, licenses and usage-descriptions; package and app builds and tests; experience-release and copy-claims steps of the released experiences; verify steps of A01-A18 on iOS 27 and 26; the app's release audits including app-licenses and app-usage-descriptions; the seven reference regression steps and the ProjectM independence check). No A19 step exists yet; the A19 copy-claims and verify steps come with G-RELEASE.

Living Wallpapers owns its domain (the project model, the curated procedural scenes and colour presets, device canvas templates with provenance, crop and safe-area guides, export requests, results, the export job and its history, the help text and copy) and UI under Packages/ExperiencesCreative/LivingWallpapers/ (Core GPU-free, CoreTests, Experience with Adapter/, ExperienceTests, Shaders, scenario-manifest.json; created in A19-P01, not present today). VisualCore owns reusable machinery: the offscreen render, read-back, render targets, encoders and capture (VisualCoreRendering), effects (VisualCoreEffects), export geometry (VisualCoreScenes), budgets (VisualCoreDiagnostics), temporary folders and documents (VisualCorePersistence), storage and the host (VisualCoreExperience, VisualCoreExperienceHost). The share paths of other experiences stay experience code and are not copied. ProjectM stays in the harness.

Reference pinned at d93edd1, read-only; scripts/run_reference_baseline.py lists the ordered reference steps; scripts/check_reference_clean.py checks the submodule; the 7 release-check steps run in two chunks via release_check.py --only (reference-engine-xcframework, reference-build-projectm-ios-sim, reference-clean; reference-test-anglerendering-ios27, reference-test-anglerendering-ios26, projectm-reference-ios27, projectm-reference-ios26), recorded in docs/apps/living-wallpapers/regression-baseline.md.

matrix.capability: Offscreen rendering: the current scene drawn at an output size independent of the screen, on the host's own context (no second context), with the pixels read back top-down

matrix.notes: Tested in OffscreenExportTests (any size, size validated first, target released on every path, live scene restored), CrossfadeSceneTests, ParticleLayerSceneTests, DepthMeshPassTests and ResourceRegistryTests. Generative Art Studio, Fluid Art Playground, Fractal Explorer, Infinite Geometry and Simulation Lab export this way.

matrix.capability: High-resolution rendering: device-sized stills (for example a tablet's 2732-pixel edge) when the GPU allows them, with the limits queried before allocation
matrix.source: brainstorm: high-resolution rendering; manual non-goal: no unlimited 8K on all devices
matrix.notes: maxRenderSize and the pixel cap are tested (OffscreenExportTests, StillCaptureTests), ExportGeometry in ExportGeometryTests. The code guarantees only the OpenGL ES 3.0 floor of 2048 per edge; real device limits are measured in A19-P05 (G-DEVICE), never assumed. Fitting each template to the reported limit with the fallback to the largest size that fits is G-TEMPLATES (A19-P01). Tiling is rejected for 0.1 (research D6). G-TEMPLATES closed in A19-P01; the row stays open for its remaining gaps. G-DEVICE closed in A19-P05 with the device-campaign plan (docs/apps/living-wallpapers/device-campaign.md, rows LW-D1 and LW-D2 pending device campaign); the per-device limit is measured there, never assumed. Available.

gaps.justification: The project model (scene, preset, template, crop, output format, animation time), export requests and results with their validation are the experience's domain, GPU-free in its Core (manual phase 01).
gaps.test: Core host tests: a request names scene, template, format and time; invalid requests refused; results record size, format and profile; project documents round-trip and migrate

gaps.justification: iPhone and iPad templates (pixel size, safe areas) are app data with a provenance record of Apple's published screen sizes; fitting a template to maxRenderSize and the pixel cap and offering the largest size that fits are app rules over ExportGeometry (manual phase 01). No tiling in 0.1.
gaps.test: Core host tests: every template has provenance; a template above the reported limit or the pixel cap is refused before allocation and the fallback is the largest even size that fits with the same aspect; fixtures at 2048, 4096 and 8192 limits

gaps.justification: Video is optional. A19-P01 decides feasibility from public APIs (encoder, disk and thermal cost, cancellation) and records the decision; any encoder is assessed for VisualCore ownership then. Until it is shown feasible no video code, copy or control exists.
gaps.test: Decision record in A19-P01 with the public API, the measured or bounded cost and the owner; a source scan finds no AVAssetWriter, VideoToolbox or video copy unless the decision is go

gaps.justification: StillImageEncoder has only pngData. JPEG and HEIC through the same ImageIO path, tagged sRGB, are generic and belong beside it in VisualCoreRendering (additive API, documentation, API baseline, reference regression).

gaps.justification: ExperienceSession.renderStill always renders at time 0. A time parameter on the session's still and on ExperienceStillRenderer (default 0, so existing callers keep their behaviour) is generic host API.

gaps.justification: The curated procedural scenes and their colour presets (shaders, fields, particles, SDFs; no images) with their license entries are the experience's content (manual phase 02).

negative.rule: Risk 1, OS wallpaper behaviour changes and third-party live wallpaper APIs are restricted. Owner: Living Wallpapers help and release (app-local G-HELP in A19-P03, G-RELEASE in A19-P06). Verification: the audit records that no public API sets the system wallpaper or installs a live wallpaper; a source scan finds no private API and no wallpaper-setting call; the A19 copy-claims step refuses 'set wallpaper', 'live wallpaper' and automatic-setting wording; the help names only the system's own controls. Release blocker: any private API, any automatic wallpaper setting, or any claim in the experience, its copy or the store text that the app sets or installs a wallpaper or exports a live wallpaper.

Risk 2, very high resolution exports cause out-of-memory. Owner: templates and the size fit (app-local G-TEMPLATES in A19-P01) over VisualCoreRendering's maxRenderSize, maxOffscreenPixels and ResourceBudget, with device limits in A19-P05 (G-DEVICE). Verification: host tests refuse every size above the reported limit or the 64,000,000-pixel cap before allocation and offer the largest size that fits; OffscreenExportTests prove the budget refusal and the release of the target on every path; the device campaign records maxRenderSize and memory per device. Release blocker: an allocation attempted above the limit, an export without a fallback, a leaked export target, or a size claim not measured on a device.

Risk 3, video encoding consumes disk and thermal budget. Owner: the video feasibility decision (app-local G-VIDEO in A19-P01; any encoder assessed for VisualCore ownership then) and the export job (G-EXPORTJOB in A19-P04). Verification: the A19-P01 decision record bounds duration, size, disk and thermal cost from public APIs; tests prove progress and cancellation remove partial files; until feasibility is shown a source scan finds no video code, copy or control. Release blocker: any video code, copy or control without a recorded go decision, a partial file left after cancellation, or a video export without progress and cancel.

reasons: A working host and an offscreen render-and-read-back path exist: RenderHost on OpenGL ES -> ANGLE -> Metal draws any RenderScene (FullScreenShaderScene, FieldPass, EffectScene, CrossfadeScene, CachedScene), and RenderHost.renderOffscreen(width:height:time:) renders it at an output size independent of the screen on the host's own context, validates the size first, reads the pixels back top-down and restores the live scene, all public and tested (OffscreenExportTests, StillRenderTests, StillCaptureTests, CrossfadeSceneTests); StillImageEncoder writes an sRGB PNG, and five experiences already share such files through the system share sheet.

8 of 26 rows are available with tests: offscreen rendering, effects and compositing, GPU budget and memory warnings, lifecycle with resize and context loss, quality tiers, licenses, the experience host and project documents with migration.

All 18 non-available rows have owned gaps: G-MODEL, G-TEMPLATES and the video feasibility decision G-VIDEO in A19-P01; the additive VisualCoreRendering encoders G-ENCODE (JPEG and HEIC tagged sRGB, verified by read-back), the additive VisualCoreExperienceHost still time G-STILLTIME and G-SCENES in A19-P02; G-EDITOR, G-HELP and G-A11Y in A19-P03; G-SAVE, G-EXPORTJOB and G-HISTORY in A19-P04; G-DEVICE in A19-P05; G-RELEASE in A19-P06. No upstream change is needed to start.

The only permission is the existing add-only Photos string through the share sheet (photo-library-add, declared in A19-P04); no PhotoKit call, no read access, no network. Living Wallpapers stays unregistered (18 registered, A01-A18) until A19-P01 creates Packages/ExperiencesCreative/LivingWallpapers with its targets and first real rules.
